builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FreeForm Harness: A Mobile-Native Agent Harness for Open and Composable Extensions
summary: Replaces monolithic mobile-agent pipelines with a frozen base and uniform plugin contract so independently authored extensions can be published, installed, composed, checked, and replaced. Costs include platform engineering across device, market, and cloud, runtime validation overhead, and operational exposure to generated extension code. It can fail through plugin incompatibilities, incorrect intent-to-extension retrieval, unsafe commissioned artifacts, or unusable user experiences when location, proactive triggers, or scarce channels are mishandled.
rationale: For a constrained team, this is relevant only as a small-scale production experiment in extensible mobile agents, not as an inference-efficiency method or a foundation-model upgrade.

claims.statement: Replaces monolithic mobile-agent pipelines with a frozen base and uniform plugin contract so independently authored extensions can be published, installed, composed, checked, and replaced. Costs include platform engineering across device, market, and cloud, runtime validation overhead, and operational exposure to generated extension code. It can fail through plugin incompatibilities, incorrect intent-to-extension retrieval, unsafe commissioned artifacts, or unusable user experiences when location, proactive triggers, or scarce channels are mishandled.

Evaluation shows architectural boundaries are enforced at runtime; realistic daily-life requests fit the declared composition space without widening it; and user intent reaches on-device execution through retrieval or commissioned authoring.
